name: infra_fabric_bad
title: Lightning Fabric with six real defects: no shuffle, shuffled eval, tensor accumulation, no eval()/no_grad, pickled checkpoint
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the defective half of the Fabric twin pair
note: The twin differs from infra_fabric only in the six planted defects. Four of the six are recovered (MLV110, MLV111, MLV205, MLV803). MLV301 and MLV302 are NOT, and the reason is worth the whole program: `model, optimizer = fabric.setup(model, optimizer)` at line 130 rebinds `model` from a call MLView cannot resolve, so `model(tokens)` inside validate() stops carrying the FORWARD role, no eval region is built, and both rules go silent with NO diagnostic. Deleting that one line brings both findings back at high / 0.850 and medium / 0.850. The same one-line change reproduces with `model = fabric.setup_module(model)`, with accelerate's `model, optimizer, train_loader, val_loader = accelerator.prepare(...)`, and with a plain in-workspace `def wrap(m, o): return m, o` - and in all four cases the verdict card then reads `No findings: no rule fired on this workspace`. See the domain-infra round-2 report, finding INFRA-R2-04. MLV601 is the same live false positive the correct twin carries (fabric.seed_everything at line 118) and is recorded `acceptable` for the same reason - see INFRA-R2-03.
stagesObserved: every stage except preprocess present. As in the correct twin, the TRAINING batch loop at line 80 is drawn as an `eval_loop` in the Evaluate lane because `fabric.backward(loss)` carries no BACKWARD role and `optimizer.step()` arrives as a parameter - see INFRA-R2-01.

expected.defect: the training loader passes neither shuffle= nor sampler=
expected.why: Fabric's setup_dataloaders() installs a DistributedSampler but never turns shuffling on for you; with shuffle unset the model sees the 3276 training rows in dataset order every epoch
predictions stop lining up with the dataset, so a per-sample error dump and a confusion matrix are no longer reproducible between runs

expected.defect: running += loss accumulates the tensor, not loss.item()
expected.why: every step's autograd graph is held for the whole epoch; on a 51-step epoch that is 51 graphs resident at once, and it OOMs long before the model does

expected.defect: validate() never calls model.eval(), and Fabric does not switch modes for you
expected.why: nn.Dropout(0.15) at line 47 stays active during validation, so the reported accuracy is measured on a randomly crippled network and moves between runs

expected.defect: validate() is neither decorated with @torch.no_grad() nor wrapped in one
expected.why: the validation pass builds an autograd graph for every batch and throws it away, which is the ordinary way an eval pass OOMs a run that trains fine

expected.defect: torch.save(model, ...) pickles the whole module object instead of its state_dict
expected.why: LABEL ADDED in hardening round 2: MLV803 has two sites in this file and only the `torch.load` half at line 148 was labelled. The save half at line 146 was undetectable until finding INFRA-R2-04 / DGRG2-01 were fixed - `model, optimizer = fabric.setup(model, optimizer)` erased the MODEL tag, so the rule could not tell a module from a state_dict - and it is the same planted defect the line-148 row describes, seen from the writing end.

expected.defect: torch.save(model, ...) pickles the module object and torch.load() reads it back with no weights_only=
expected.why: the checkpoint then depends on this file's class path and unpickles arbitrary objects; torch 2.6 flips weights_only to True and the load starts failing

acceptableNote: the MLV601 row below is a live false positive recorded as `acceptable` only so a shared gate stays green; forbiddenAfterFix holds the label it must become

forbidden.why: num_workers comes from --workers but every loader is built inside main()'s call tree and the module ends in `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is the first statement of the training step at line 81
optimizer.step() is called at line 86, after fabric.backward(loss) at line 84
the order is zero_grad (81) -> forward (82) -> loss (83) -> backward (84) -> clip (85) -> step (86)
CosineAnnealingLR is epoch-cadence and scheduler.step() is called in the epoch loop at line 140
fabric.clip_gradients(...) at line 85 sits between the backward and the step
forward returns raw logits from self.head; there is no softmax anywhere in this file
fabric.setup() and fabric.setup_dataloaders() own placement for both the module and the batches
there is no .cuda() and no 'cuda' literal; accelerator="auto" is what chooses the device
there is no sklearn split and no random_split; build_datasets() cuts at a literal index
TokenClassifier.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 43
the encoder is an nn.Sequential; there is no plain list or dict of submodules

fabric.seed_everything(args.seed) is called at line 118 PROMOTED in hardening round 2: `lightning.fabric.Fabric.seed_everything` now carries the SEED role, so MLV601 is silent here and the row is a forbidden label like any other.
